A DRIP AND A RING: a single drip falling from the tallest icicle and landing bright, rings spreading slowly out across the still pool
THE DROP AT THE TIP: one bright drop hanging at an icicle's tip, perfectly round, catching every color in the chamber before letting go
RINGS TO THE EDGE: the rings from one fallen drip reaching outward and touching the pool's scalloped lip, soft and even
ONE BRIGHT LANDING: a single drip landing on the still water and ringing out, the sound and the circle going together
THE DROP ABOUT TO FALL: one bright drop trembling at an icicle's tip, round and full, holding the whole chamber's glow inside it
LIGHT ON THE FROZEN SHAPE: the light just reaching the frozen shape set deep in the wall and lifting it gently out of the dark
THE WARM PATCH CLIMBING: a warm patch of light climbing one ice step and stopping there, resting golden on the blue
LIGHT AT THE LONG TIP: the glow just touching the longest icicle's tip and kindling a small bright point at its end
LIGHT FINDING THE WALL: light moving slowly along the ice wall and finding a pocket of frozen bubbles, each one glowing
FROST SLIDING SOFT: a slab of frost sliding off a ledge and breaking soft on the floor in a small bright heap
THE WHOLE ICICLE DOWN: one long icicle just come away and lying whole on the ice, every chunky stepped side still perfect
POWDER FROM THE ROOF: a small fall of powder letting go from the roof above and settling in a fine bright ring below
THE SLAB LANDS GENTLY: a curved slab of frost sliding from its ledge and coming to rest on the floor, barely a sound
ONE CRYSTAL TURNING: a single bright ice crystal turning over slowly as it falls past the near edge, catching light on every face
FROST LIFTING: frost lifting off a ledge in a slow turning cloud, each piece catching a different color as it goes
THE LONE FLAKE: one flake coming down through the whole chamber alone, taking its time, drifting left and then right
A CRYSTAL PAST THE EDGE: a small bright crystal tumbling gently past the near edge, spinning, going dim, then bright again
A NEW CRACK REACHING: a new white crack reaching out across the floor ice and stopping, clean and fine as a drawn line
THE LINE UNDER THE FLOOR: a thin white line running out under the clear floor ice, branching once and then going still
A WEB OF NEW CRACKS: a fine web of new cracks reaching out from one old one, spreading in a delicate bright pattern
THE CRACK THAT STOPS: a pale crack finding its way across the ice and stopping just short of the pool's edge, quiet and decided
A BUBBLE AT THE SURFACE: a bubble rising through the still pool and breaking the surface with the softest possible sound
THE MIST THINNING: the mist thinning away to nothing, leaving the chamber clear and every icicle sharply bright
THE POOL GOING STILL: the pool going glassy still again, holding the ceiling and all its icicles perfectly inside itself
THE LAST RING FADING: a last ring fading out across the water, growing pale and wide until it is gone and the pool is glassy still again
